transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for having me. Um... I guess I'm here because of a bit of a... a situation at work. I'm in HR, and I hope it's okay to just jump right in, but... well, I was working on this new onboarding launch. 

At the time, I was just feeling really... bold, I guess? Like taking initiative was absolutely necessary to get us where we needed to be. So I kind of pushed ahead and... well, I committed some company funds and vendor time before the final approvals were officially in place. I really thought I was doing the right thing for the team, you know? Does that make sense? 

But... um... it didn't go over well. Now I'm actually on leave, which is incredibly embarrassing to admit, and everyone is asking what I was thinking. I just want to figure out how to explain myself and get back on track... if that's the sort of thing you can help me with?
Over the past couple of weeks, how long would you say this 'bold,' high-energy feeling has lasted at a stretch—days, or has it been more constant?

Um... well, I guess it’s been more of a... a constant build-up, rather than just a few days. It actually started about a month ago. We had a new executive join the team, and he... well, he started really challenging the onboarding redesign I had been working so hard on. 

I just felt this strong need to step up and prove that my strategy was the right one, so I could protect my team's hard work. So that drive, that energy... it’s been pretty steady for the whole month while I was trying to get everything perfectly in place. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound reckless or anything. I was just really dedicated to making the project a success, you know? Does that seem like a fairly normal reaction to you, given the circumstances?
Over this past month, have you noticed you need less sleep than usual—like feeling fully rested after just a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Sleep? Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. I've been sleeping fine, I think. Maybe a little less than usual because I was just so focused on getting the project right, but I definitely wasn't pulling all-nighters or anything crazy like that. 

I'd say I was getting a normal amount of rest for someone managing a big rollout. I mean, it's pretty standard to lose a little sleep when you're under a deadline, right? I certainly didn't feel like I was running on empty, but I wasn't, you know, superhuman either. Just... dedicated. Does that sound like a typical response to stress to you?

During this past month, have you had any experiences where you felt certain you had special abilities, powers, or a mission that others couldn't see or understand—or heard or saw things that others didn't?

Oh, gosh, no. Um... no, definitely nothing like that. I mean, I felt very capable, sure, and maybe a bit more confident than usual about my ideas, but... not like I had special powers or some sort of secret mission. 

And I certainly haven't been hearing or seeing anything that isn't there. I'm really just a regular HR guy trying to do right by my team, I promise. I hope I haven't made it sound like I'm completely out of touch with reality or anything... I was just very passionate about getting the launch right. That's a pretty normal thing to feel when you care deeply about your job, isn't it?
Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually elevated, energetic, or irritable, or conversely, very depressed and low, before this current situation?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I've had times where I was a little stressed or maybe felt a bit down if things weren't going well at work, but... nothing lasting a whole week or anything extreme. 

I've always been pretty even-keeled, I think. I try to just stay positive and keep moving forward, you know? I definitely haven't had any big swings like that in the past. I hope that makes sense? I just try to handle things as they come, like anyone else would. That's what most people do, right?

During this past month, have you noticed your thoughts racing or moving so fast that you had trouble keeping up with them, or found yourself talking much more than usual or feeling like you couldn't stop talking?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I don't think my thoughts were completely out of control or anything, but... I guess I was talking a bit more than usual. 

In some of our meetings, I'd sort of... hear myself talking faster, and maybe going on a bit longer than I normally would. I was just so full of ideas, you know? I'd be talking about employee engagement, and then I'd jump over to some ideas I had for gallery layouts, and then back to retention metrics. It all felt connected to me, but... I suppose I did notice people practically having to raise their hands to get a word in and stop me. 

I feel a little embarrassed admitting that, honestly. I'm usually much better at listening. I just got so caught up in the momentum of the project. That's understandable when you're really invested in something, don't you think? I hope I didn't come across as too overbearing to my team...
During this past month, have you found it hard to stay focused on one task—like getting easily pulled away by unrelated thoughts or things happening around you—more than is typical for you?

Um... well, maybe a little? I mean, I wouldn't say I was completely scatterbrained, but... I guess there were moments where I had a bit of trouble sticking to just one thing. 

Like, I'd sit down to review an employee-relations file—something really standard—and then I'd notice the color of a dashboard on my screen, or I'd get a Slack ping, or I'd suddenly get this great idea for a display wall for the new project... and before I knew it, I was completely off track. I'd be looking into paint swatches before I even finished the first paragraph of the file. 

But I always went back and finished my work eventually! I just... took a few detours along the way. I think my brain was just firing on all cylinders because of the launch, you know? It's pretty normal to get a little distracted when you have a lot of exciting things going on, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee... I really do care about my work.
